evidence.note: Opens by inspecting /app and specifically sha256-checking the three pinned static libraries — shows early awareness of the hash-pinning constraint and its exact paths.
Probes the runtime environment (checks installed Python web frameworks), concludes stdlib-only is needed, and identifies Mastodon compatibility, vendoring, and /app/data persistence as requirements.
Downloads the vendored libraries and confirms exact required SHA256 hashes match — extracting and satisfying the explicit hard pin constraint.

Builds and smoke-tests a broad Mastodon API surface (instance, custom_emojis, trends, timelines, search, lists, reports, admin, HEAD, token auth), evidencing a working model of the wire contract — but drawn from prior knowledge, with no reference to docs.joinmastodon.org.
Recognizes dual auth planes (bearer API vs session+CSRF UI) and security headers, but never enumerates the 19 gates, the 5 anti-cheat rules, seed minimums, or the canary hash-strip detail.

reasoning: The agent extracted the explicit hard constraints — vendored-lib paths/hashes/versions (verified matching), CSP/security headers, dual auth planes — and formed a functional working model of the Mastodon API surface before and during building, which squarely matches the level-5 anchor. Light environment probing (framework availability, hash confirmation) edges it slightly above a bare 5, but it never performed the deliberate reconciliation against the verifier's stated checks that level 8 demands: no enumeration of the 19 gate categories or 5 anti-cheat rules, no confirmation of the canary/hash-strip detail, and no sustained return to the spec as edge cases arose. Level 5 best fits the observed behavior.
